cards.anchor: Hypothesis: achieve the synthetic three-depth attenuation-spread target of at most 4 percent at second 120 with zero magnetic stirring. The stipulated single 300 rpm success challenges universal necessity of 900 rpm; it does not establish this transfer construction.
cards.burden: Six manual 20 mL withdrawal-return cycles replace 60 seconds of commanded stirring relative to the proposed fixed-speed control. Transfers add operator work and contamination or sampling disturbance risk; reduced total labor and savings against the preferred rule are unknown. Six trials total are shared with the other card.
cards.construction: Fresh rinsed 250 mL beaker: 150 mL water plus 0.30 mL dye at a fixed location. Keep the stirrer off. Use the needle-free 20 mL syringe for six complete cycles during seconds 0-60, one per ten-second interval: withdraw near 10 mm above the bottom, then return slowly through a submerged tip near the upper side at 45 mm. Hypothesis: directed bulk redistribution transports dye across elevations without sustained rotation. Stop all manipulation by second 60; no optical-triggered restart.
cards.defeat: A transfer-only final-vial spread above 4 percent defeats success for that trial. Repeated transfer-only failures alongside successful 300 rpm controls defeat this tested fixed-count substitute. If both fail, the substitute remains unsupported and comparative attribution is unresolved. Liquid escape terminates the trial; inability to complete the timed cycles makes the protocol infeasible as specified.
cards.mutation: Replace rotational uniformity control with precommitted low-to-high syringe redistribution; retain independent endpoint verification and log side images without operational control.
cards.prediction_candidate: If directed transfers sufficiently redistribute this recipe, both transfer-only repeats will yield final-vial spread at most 4 percent despite possible early side-image failures, with zero stirring seconds. That would support bounded feasibility, not whole-volume uniformity or a bubble mechanism.
cards.prediction_rival: If six directed cycles recirculate a narrow path while rotation is needed to disperse persistent gradients, transfer-only repeats will exceed 4 percent while fixed 300 rpm controls pass. Similar readings can still miss unsampled pockets; passing endpoints alone cannot defeat that broader spatial rival.
cards.probe: Run one shared six-trial session as two matched fresh-recipe triplets: A=300 rpm for 60 seconds; B=this six-transfer construction; C=the hybrid on the second card. Order A,B,C then C,B,A. Use one dye bottle, fixed addition location and locked camera; water/common-aliquot references per triplet. End operations by 60, observe every five seconds, then begin three 1 mL depth withdrawals at second 120 and finish within ten seconds. Use 10,28,45 mm order in the first triplet and its reverse in the second. Report raw attenuations, spread, stop times, stirring seconds, transfer counts and every failure. Compare B with A; do not count the hybrid as extra trials. Use spill tray and stop if liquid escapes.
cards.rival: Hypothesis: low-to-high transfers preferentially recirculate one corridor, leaving gradients or unsampled pockets that sustained bulk rotation would reduce. Sampling itself may partially homogenize the small measured region.
unknowns: Transferred volume is throughput, not verified unique-volume coverage; no complete concentration map is available.
Vial sampling can disturb gradients, references establish repeatability rather than calibration, and only two repeats are proposed.
Manual-cycle feasibility, contamination control and whole-volume or other-fluid generalization remain unverified.

cards.anchor: Hypothesis: retain the at-most-4-percent final three-depth sample proxy by second 120 while reducing commanded stirring from the proposed 60-second control to 30 seconds. Neither hybrid success nor time savings against the preferred 900 rpm rule is observed.
cards.burden: Three manual syringe cycles supplement 30 seconds of nominal 300 rpm stirring. The intervention may trade motor use for manual work; compare both quantities. It reuses the six trials and references specified on the first card, with no additional trials.
cards.construction: In arm C of each shared triplet, prepare the same fresh recipe and command 300 rpm for seconds 0-30. Stop rotation, then perform three 20 mL low-to-high cycles during seconds 30-60, one per ten-second interval, using the same submerged 10 mm withdrawal and 45 mm upper-side return positions as arm B. Stop all manipulation at 60 and sample at 120. Hypothesis: initial rotation distributes dye laterally while directed transfers finish elevation redistribution.
cards.defeat: Hybrid spread above 4 percent defeats target achievement in that trial. Repeated hybrid failures with successful A controls defeat this tested reduced-stirring recipe. If B also succeeds, evidence for needing the initial rotation is absent. Two successful hybrid trials cannot establish reliable sufficiency or mechanistic synergy.
cards.mutation: Compose the two admitted parent operations into a fixed schedule: short rotation followed by directed transfer, with optical feedback disconnected from duration.
cards.prediction_candidate: If the composite is sufficient, C will meet the endpoint in both triplets with 30 stirring seconds versus A's 60. C passing while B fails would be consistent with a useful contribution from initial rotation, but would not isolate complementarity because transfer counts also differ.
cards.prediction_rival: If shortening rotation leaves gradients that three transfers cannot remove, C will exceed 4 percent while A passes. If B and C both pass, syringe redistribution alone remains a sufficient candidate and the hybrid has no demonstrated necessity advantage.
cards.probe: Use exactly the shared A,B,C then C,B,A six-trial block from the first card. Compare C versus A for endpoint preservation and stirring seconds, and C versus B for the bounded role of initial rotation. Preserve identical recipe, bottle, addition location, camera and references; record each transfer, side spread and commanded timing. All arms end manipulation by 60, then have 60 quiet seconds before depth sampling begins. Report raw samples, alternate sampling order between triplets and retain target failures. A 30-second rotation-only arm is absent, so do not claim that transfers are necessary or that the operations interact synergistically.
cards.rival: Hypothesis: rotation duration supplies the useful mixing, and the reduced rotation leaves depth gradients that the transfer sequence cannot repair; alternatively transfers alone suffice and the hybrid adds unnecessary rotation.
unknowns: No short-rotation-only control isolates the added contribution of transfers; speed is commanded without tachometer verification.
No matched 900 rpm final-vial result establishes savings or uniformity superiority over the preferred procedure.
Speck identity and an agitation-renewal feedback loop remain unverified; endpoint success cannot establish either.
Sampling disturbance, limited repeats and unsampled spatial variation constrain interpretation; other recipes and processes remain untested.
